Classification guard: the authored edge asserts association only (etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, hypothesizedOnly:true, mechanismCategory PSYCHOPHYSIOLOGICAL). Both located studies are cross-sectional questionnaire surveys without pre-lesion baselines or diagnostic interviews, so individual claims require separate clinical documentation of a depressive disorder, a chronology relative to the keloid, symptom and treatment burden, and assessment of competing psychosocial contributors, with review by a qualified medical professional.

Constitutive identity guard: no keloids-to-scars edge is authored - a keloid IS a scar, and the catalog's scars identity (Scars, Painful or Unstable) is the rating view of the lesion itself rather than a distinct downstream consequence, so an edge would restate the identity. The psychiatric window follows the alopecia-areata, vitiligo, acne-scarring, and hidradenitis-suppurativa precedents at association-only strength.

Duplicate-scope and boundary guards: the depressive-disorder identity already receives sixty-six windows, so the target is not pre-empted and this adds the keloid-specific dermatologic window; no anxiety-disorder edge is authored because the located anxiety signal in the Huang 2025 model tracks pain symptoms, income, self-efficacy, and coping style rather than the lesion itself and the conservative standard defers it pending independent evidence; no contractures edge is authored (the located contracture literature is burn, congenital-naevus, and neuromuscular-specific - zero-record for keloid); no squamous-cell-carcinoma edge is authored (a single keloid-in-scar case report was retrieved, PMID 31065195, and the Marjolin evidence concentrates in burn scars - zero-record and magnitude guards); no unexplained-chronic-pain edge is authored because keloid pain and pruritus are lesion-explained.
governanceNotes: D1 batch 50 (2026-09-24): one bounded association edge authored - keloids to depressive-disorder (rank 1) - classified ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, and hypothesizedOnly:true; mechanismCategory PSYCHOPHYSIOLOGICAL. The proposition rests on the Huang 2025 study of 202 Chinese patients with keloids, which states that in addition to producing pain and itching keloids can cause psychological symptoms including anxiety and depression and reports mean Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale scores of 9.82 +/- 2.20 for anxiety and 7.96 +/- 2.70 for depression, with HADS depression significantly associated with use of social support (odds ratio 0.607) and coping tendencies partially mediating the relationship between social support and depression (38.58% of the total effect); it rests also on the Lu 2021 study of quality of life and psychosocial wellbeing in Chinese patients with keloids using the Dermatology Life Quality Index and the Symptom Checklist-90, which found interpersonal-sensitivity, depression, and anxiety scores higher in the visible-scar group than in either the invisible-scar group or the normal group (P < .05), higher depression and anxiety scores in the invisible-scar group than in the normal group (P < .05), and a greater effect on female patients' mental health (P < .05). A reproducible depressive-symptom burden is thus documented in keloid-specific populations.

Counter-evidence and caveat screens recorded 2026-09-24: (i) cross-sectional design - neither study establishes temporal precedence, so pre-existing depressive disorder may precede the keloid and the direction is not asserted; (ii) instrument rather than diagnosis - both use questionnaire scales (HADS, SCL-90) rather than structured diagnostic interviews, and the Huang depression mean sits at rather than clearly beyond common screening cut-offs, so the edge records a symptom burden rather than a diagnosed disorder; (iii) mediator structure - depression in the located model is partially mediated by social support and coping style and associated with pain symptoms and income, so lesion-independent psychosocial factors contribute; (iv) population scope - both cohorts are Chinese and the Lu study distinguishes visible from invisible lesions, so the signal is strongest for disfiguring lesions and is not uniform across sites.

Negative screens recorded 2026-09-24: (i) no keloids-to-scars edge - constitutive identity guard (a keloid is a scar and the scars identity is the lesion's own rating view); (ii) no anxiety-disorder edge - the located anxiety signal tracks pain, income, self-efficacy, and coping style rather than the lesion itself and is deferred pending independent keloid-specific evidence; (iii) no keloids-to-contractures edge - the located contracture literature concerns burns, giant congenital naevi, and neuromuscular disease rather than keloids (zero-record guard); (iv) no keloids-to-squamous-cell-carcinoma edge - one case report of carcinoma arising in a keloid scar was retrieved while the Marjolin evidence concentrates in burn scars (zero-record and magnitude guards); (v) no keloids-to-unexplained-chronic-pain edge - keloid pain and pruritus are lesion-explained and that identity is reserved for unexplained presentations (identity-boundary guard); (vi) no loss-of-eyebrow, scarring-alopecia, or other adnexal edge - zero-record for this identity.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The Huang 2025 study of 202 Chinese patients with keloids, which states that in addition to producing pain and itching keloids can cause psychological symptoms including anxiety and depression, reports mean Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale scores of 9.82 +/- 2.20 for anxiety and 7.96 +/- 2.70 for depression, with HADS depression significantly associated with use of social support (odds ratio 0.607) and coping tendencies partially mediating the relationship between social support and depression (38.58% of the total effect); the Lu 2021 study of quality of life and psychosocial wellbeing in Chinese patients with keloids using the Dermatology Life Quality Index and the Symptom Checklist-90 found interpersonal-sensitivity, depression, and anxiety scores higher in the visible-scar group than in either the invisible-scar group or the normal group (P < .05), higher depression and anxiety scores in the invisible-scar group than in the normal group (P < .05) while other indices did not differ, and a greater effect on female patients' mental health (P < .05); the literature documents a reproducible depressive-symptom burden in keloid patients without establishing that the keloid caused an individual's depressive disorder.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: The mapping does not assert that keloids caused an individual's depressive disorder: the located studies are cross-sectional questionnaire surveys without a pre-keloid baseline, so direction cannot be established and pre-existing depression may precede the lesion; the instruments are screening scales rather than diagnostic interviews and some group means sit near rather than clearly beyond common cut-offs; disfigurement, pain, pruritus, treatment burden, and surgical history independently affect mood; and the depression signal is partially mediated by social support and coping style - so individual claims require a documented depressive disorder with chronology relative to the keloid and assessment of competing psychosocial contributors.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized psychosocial-burden route is described: a keloid is a visible, raised, persistently symptomatic lesion in a cosmetically and functionally sensitive site that produces pain, itching, and disfigurement, prompts repeated and often disappointing treatments, and alters body image, self-perception, and social participation; the resulting chronic stress, interpersonal sensitivity, and reduced quality of life are proposed to contribute to depressive symptoms, with social support and coping style acting as partial mediators in the located model. Because the surveys are cross-sectional and lesion and mood are measured at one point, the individual causal direction remains a hypothesis.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. Keloid-specific surveys document higher depression scores and worse dermatology quality of life, but individual determination requires separate clinical documentation of a depressive disorder, a chronology relative to the keloid's onset, assessment of pain and pruritus severity, and consideration of competing psychosocial contributors, with review by a qualified medical professional.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Dermatologic documentation of the keloid(s) with site, size, number, duration, growth history, prior treatments, and any pain or pruritus; psychiatric or psychological documentation of a depressive disorder with onset, duration, and the diagnostic criteria met using validated measures or a diagnostic interview rather than screening questionnaires alone; chronology establishing whether depressive symptoms preceded or followed the keloid and any treatment for it; documentation of functional, occupational, and social impact attributable to the lesion; assessment of competing contributors including chronic pain or other dermatologic disease, disfigurement from other causes, substance use, prior psychiatric history, and psychosocial stressors; qualified behavioural-health assessment of whether the keloid materially contributed to the depressive disorder
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Primary or recurrent depressive disorder independent of the keloid
Chronic pain from another source (musculoskeletal, neuropathic, or other dermatologic disease)
Body dysmorphic disorder or another primary psychiatric disorder
Adjustment disorder related to a non-dermatologic stressor
Medical or pharmacological contributors (hypothyroidism, anaemia, corticosteroids, interferon)

evidenceGaps: Dermatologic documentation of the keloid(s) with site, size, number, duration, growth history, prior treatments, and any pain or pruritus; psychiatric or psychological documentation of a depressive disorder with onset, duration, and the diagnostic criteria met using validated measures or a diagnostic interview rather than screening questionnaires alone; chronology establishing whether depressive symptoms preceded or followed the keloid and any treatment for it; documentation of functional, occupational, and social impact attributable to the lesion; assessment of competing contributors including chronic pain or other dermatologic disease, disfigurement from other causes, substance use, prior psychiatric history, and psychosocial stressors; qualified behavioural-health assessment of whether the keloid materially contributed to the depressive disorder
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY: a 202 keloid-patient survey reports mean HADS anxiety and depression scores of 9.82 and 7.96 with depression associated with social support and partially mediated by coping style, and a comparative keloid survey reports higher Symptom Checklist-90 depression, anxiety, and interpersonal-sensitivity scores than controls, greatest with visible lesions and in women. Both are cross-sectional questionnaire studies without diagnostic interviews or pre-lesion baselines, so the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only, matching the alopecia-areata, vitiligo, acne-scarring, and hidradenitis-suppurativa windows already on the depressive-disorder identity.
